commit_message:
[Vulkan] Preserve normalized memory type across host import compat query

In iree_hal_vulkan_allocator_import_buffer,
iree_hal_vulkan_allocator_normalize_host_allocation_import_params normalized
compat_params (0x56) from IREE internal's req to vulkan requirements. The 6th
bit (strict host local) is dropped here (0x16).

Later on iree_hal_vulkan_allocator_query_buffer_compatibility, the 5th bit is
flipped to 1 (0x36).

In the call trace of runtime/src/iree/hal/drivers/vulkan/allocator.c:936 ->
runtime/src/iree/hal/drivers/vulkan/allocator.c:952 ->
runtime/src/iree/hal/drivers/vulkan/allocator.c:892, on the i=5 iteration, it
fails the iree_all_bits_set check on the 5th bit exactly, leading to
iree_hal_vulkan_allocator_resolve_memory_placement ultimately return false and
fail the test.

The cause is iree_hal_vulkan_allocator_query_buffer_compatibility overriding
compat_params, trying to satisfy the memory request from compat_params,
rewriting compat_params' type in the process to the best memory type that the
GPU actually support, which unfortunately causes a mismatch later down the line.

Fix: keep the query's coercion of compat_params but restore the normalized
memory type afterwards, so placement selects among the types the host pointer
allows.

Tested on:
- OS: NixOS 26.11, Linux 6.18.48
- CPU: AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D
- GPUs: AMD Radeon iGPU (PCI 1002:13c0, amdgpu) and
  NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti (driver 610.57.04)
- Vulkan driver: Mesa 26.2.1 RADV (libvulkan_radeon.so)
- direnv (.envrc): export VK_LOADER_DRIVERS_SELECT='radeon_icd*'
  (local only: NVIDIA driver 610.57.04 miscompiles Vulkan tests, so the
  AMD GPU is used)

Before:
  $ cmake --build ../iree-build --target runtime/src/iree/hal/drivers/vulkan/cts/all
  $ ctest --test-dir ../iree-build -R vulkan/cts -j8
  98% tests passed, 1 tests failed out of 44
    1405 - iree/hal/drivers/vulkan/cts/buffer_tests (Failed)
  $ ../iree-build/runtime/src/iree/hal/drivers/vulkan/cts/buffer_tests --gtest_filter='*ImportHostAllocation*'
  [ RUN      ] CTS/AllocatorTest.ImportHostAllocationNullCallback/vulkan
  ...allocator.c:2131: INVALID_ARGUMENT; allocator cannot find a Vulkan memory
  type compatible with the imported host pointer
  [  FAILED  ] CTS/AllocatorTest.ImportHostAllocationNullCallback/vulkan
  [ RUN      ] CTS/AllocatorTest.ImportHostAllocationWithCallback/vulkan
  ...allocator.c:2131: INVALID_ARGUMENT; allocator cannot find a Vulkan memory
  type compatible with the imported host pointer
  [  FAILED  ] CTS/AllocatorTest.ImportHostAllocationWithCallback/vulkan
  [  PASSED  ] 0 tests.
  [  FAILED  ] 2 tests

After:
  $ cmake --build ../iree-build --target runtime/src/iree/hal/drivers/vulkan/cts/all
  $ ctest --test-dir ../iree-build -R vulkan/cts -j8
  100% tests passed out of 44
  $ ../iree-build/runtime/src/iree/hal/drivers/vulkan/cts/buffer_tests --gtest_filter='*ImportHostAllocation*'
  [ RUN      ] CTS/AllocatorTest.ImportHostAllocationNullCallback/vulkan
  [       OK ] CTS/AllocatorTest.ImportHostAllocationNullCallback/vulkan
  [ RUN      ] CTS/AllocatorTest.ImportHostAllocationWithCallback/vulkan
  [       OK ] CTS/AllocatorTest.ImportHostAllocationWithCallback/vulkan
  [  PASSED  ] 2 tests.

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Add an option to limit the bytes a dispatch binds (#25299)

Some targets need to have every buffer a dispatch binds mapped to a
limited address space, e.g. 32 bit. There may also be other limits on
the amount of mapped memory at the same time. Fusion can form dispatches
that cannot run, even when each binding fits into the max allocation
size. For instance, once a large constant is split into shards (see
`iree-global-opt-split-large-constants`), elementwise fusion merges the
per-shard embedding lookups back into one op that reads every shard.

This adds `--iree-dispatch-creation-max-dispatch-binding-size` (default
0, no limit) and a `max-dispatch-binding-size` option on the passes that
grow dispatches:

* ElementwiseOpFusion, for fusion outside of dispatches,
* FuseMultiUseElementwiseProducer, for fusion outside of dispatches,
* FormDispatchRegions, in `FusionGroup::wouldExceedOperandLimit`, next
to the existing limit on the number of operands, so that all producer
and consumer fusion decisions are covered,
* CloneProducersIntoDispatchRegions, through
`CloneableIntoDispatchOptions` in `getCloneableOps`,
* FuseHorizontalContractions, which adds a weight and a result to the
  fused contraction for each contraction it merges,
* ConvertTensorToFlow, for producers cloned into the dispatches it
  creates for slices.

The bytes are estimated by `IREE::Flow::getDispatchBindingBytes`: the
statically shaped tensors that the ops read from outside (as operands or
captured in their regions), plus their results that are used outside.
Loads of the same global count once; `tensor.empty`, `linalg.fill` and
splat constants are not bindings. Producers cloned into a dispatch
contribute only what they read, because those remain in place for their
other users. Fusion decisions count the producers that
CloneProducersIntoDispatchRegions will clone into the dispatch later
(e.g. dequantization ops) by what they read, not by their results. A
fusion or clone is refused only if the dispatch would then bind more
than the limit and more than it did without it, so fusions that shrink a
dispatch already over the limit still happen.

Dynamically shaped tensors count as zero bytes, so the limit only covers
static shapes, which includes all constants.

download the test artifacts from Azure (`AuthorizationFailure`), and
main (14e6942619) fails the same way.

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Add an option to limit the bytes a dispatch binds (#25299)

Some targets need to have every buffer a dispatch binds mapped to a
limited address space, e.g. 32 bit. There may also be other limits on
the amount of mapped memory at the same time. Fusion can form dispatches
that cannot run, even when each binding fits into the max allocation
size. For instance, once a large constant is split into shards (see
`iree-global-opt-split-large-constants`), elementwise fusion merges the
per-shard embedding lookups back into one op that reads every shard.

This adds `--iree-dispatch-creation-max-dispatch-binding-size` (default
0, no limit) and a `max-dispatch-binding-size` option on the passes that
grow dispatches:

* ElementwiseOpFusion, for fusion outside of dispatches,
* FuseMultiUseElementwiseProducer, for fusion outside of dispatches,
* FormDispatchRegions, in `FusionGroup::wouldExceedOperandLimit`, next
to the existing limit on the number of operands, so that all producer
and consumer fusion decisions are covered,
* CloneProducersIntoDispatchRegions, through
`CloneableIntoDispatchOptions` in `getCloneableOps`,
* FuseHorizontalContractions, which adds a weight and a result to the
  fused contraction for each contraction it merges,
* ConvertTensorToFlow, for producers cloned into the dispatches it
  creates for slices.

The bytes are estimated by `IREE::Flow::getDispatchBindingBytes`: the
statically shaped tensors that the ops read from outside (as operands or
captured in their regions), plus their results that are used outside.
Loads of the same global count once; `tensor.empty`, `linalg.fill` and
splat constants are not bindings. Producers cloned into a dispatch
contribute only what they read, because those remain in place for their
other users. Fusion decisions count the producers that
CloneProducersIntoDispatchRegions will clone into the dispatch later
(e.g. dequantization ops) by what they read, not by their results. A
fusion or clone is refused only if the dispatch would then bind more
than the limit and more than it did without it, so fusions that shrink a
dispatch already over the limit still happen.

Dynamically shaped tensors count as zero bytes, so the limit only covers
static shapes, which includes all constants.

Co-authored-by: Author: Tim Jammer <jammer@roofline.ai>

grow dispatches:

* ElementwiseOpFusion, for fusion outside of dispatches,
* FuseMultiUseElementwiseProducer, for fusion outside of dispatches,
* FormDispatchRegions, in `FusionGroup::wouldExceedOperandLimit`, next
to the existing limit on the number of operands, so that all producer
and consumer fusion decisions are covered,
* CloneProducersIntoDispatchRegions, through
`CloneableIntoDispatchOptions` in `getCloneableOps`,
* FuseHorizontalContractions, which adds a weight and a result to the
  fused contraction for each contraction it merges,
* ConvertTensorToFlow, for producers cloned into the dispatches it
  creates for slices.

The bytes are estimated by `IREE::Flow::getDispatchBindingBytes`: the
statically shaped tensors that the ops read from outside (as operands or
captured in their regions), plus their results that are used outside.
Loads of the same global count once; `tensor.empty`, `linalg.fill` and
splat constants are not bindings. Producers cloned into a dispatch
contribute only what they read, because those remain in place for their
other users. Fusion decisions count the producers that
CloneProducersIntoDispatchRegions will clone into the dispatch later
(e.g. dequantization ops) by what they read, not by their results. A
fusion or clone is refused only if the dispatch would then bind more
than the limit and more than it did without it, so fusions that shrink a
dispatch already over the limit still happen.

Dynamically shaped tensors count as zero bytes, so the limit only covers
static shapes, which includes all constants.
